label: obs-reg-vertremoval-deg
title: Observation
body_md:
\label{obs-reg-vertremoval-deg}
    Let $G$ be a connected $d$-regular graph for some $d$. Let $v \in V(G)$. Then every connected component of $G-v$ is $(d-1)$-degenerate.
head: environment

label: lem-highlow2
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $V_{\operatorname*{high}}$ and $V_{\operatorname*{low}}$ partition $V(G)$, we have that $|V_{\operatorname*{high}}| + |V_{\operatorname*{low}}| = |V(G)|$.
Now we suppose toward a contradiction that $|V_{\operatorname*{low}}| < \frac{q}{k + q}|V(G)|$.
Then $$|V_{\operatorname*{high}}| = |V(G)| - |V_{\operatorname*{low}}| > |V(G)| - \frac{q}{k + q}|V(G)|.$$
Since $\deg_G^\ell(v) \geq \frac{k + q}{2}$ for any $v \in V_{\operatorname*{high}}$, we get that
  \begin{align*}
    |E(G)| \geq \sum_{v \in V_{\operatorname*{high}}} \deg_G^\ell(v) &> \left(|V(G)| - \frac{q}{k + q}|V(G)|\right) \left(\frac{k+q}{2}\right) \\
    &= \left(\frac{k}{k+q}|V(G)|\right)\left(\frac{k + q}{2} \right) = \frac{k}{2}|V(G)|,
  \end{align*}
which contradicts that $|E(G)| \leq \frac{k}{2}|V(G)|$, by definition of $k$. Hence, $|V_{\operatorname*{low}}| \geq \frac{q}{k+q}|V(G)|$.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md: Notice that the maximum degree $\Delta$ is always a valid choice for $k$ in~\Cref{lem-highlow2}, as it is always true that $|E(G)| \leq \frac{\Delta}{2}|V(G)|$. Thus, for any $q < \Delta$,~\Cref{lem-highlow2} implies that the number of vertices with left degree strictly less than $\frac{\Delta + q}{2}$ is at least $\frac{q}{\Delta + q}|V(G)|$.

label: lem-kdeg2
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem-kdeg2}
    Let $G$ be a $d$-degenerate graph of maximum degree~$\Delta\geq 3$, with $d,q < \Delta$. 
    Let~$L$ be any $\Delta$-list assignment for $G$.
    Then $G$ has at least 
    $\left(\left\lfloor\frac{\Delta-q}{2}\right\rfloor + 1\right)^{\frac{q}{\Delta+q}|V(G)|}$ 
    $L$-colorings.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $G$ be a $d$-degenerate graph for some $d < \Delta$.
  We fix a $d$-degeneracy ordering $\sigma = v_1, \dots, v_n$  of the vertices.
  We partition the vertices of $G$ based on their left degree.
  Let $V_{\operatorname*{high}} = \{v: \frac{\Delta+ q}{2} \leq \deg_G^\ell(v) \}$, and let 
  $V_{\operatorname*{low}} = \{v: 0 \leq \deg_G^\ell(v) <  \frac{\Delta+q}{2} \}$.
      By Lemma~\ref{lem-highlow2}, setting $k = \Delta$, we have $|V_{\operatorname*{low}}| \geq \frac{q}{\Delta+q}|V(G)|$.

  We count the number of colorings by processing the vertices in the order of $\sigma$, going from left to right.
  For a vertex $v_i$, we can choose among at least $\Delta- \deg_G^\ell(v_i)$ colors.
  If $v_i \in V_{\operatorname*{high}}$, there are thus at least $\Delta- d\geq 1$ colors available.
   If $v_i \in V_{\operatorname*{low}}$, there are strictly more than $\Delta - \frac{\Delta+q}{2}$ colors available. 
  Thus, for a vertex $v_i \in V_{\operatorname*{low}}$, there are at least $\lfloor \Delta - \frac{\Delta+q}{2}\rfloor + 1$ colors available.
  
   Hence, the number of $L$-colorings is at least
  \[
    \left(\left\lfloor\Delta - \frac{\Delta+q}{2}\right\rfloor + 1\right)^{|V_{\operatorname*{low}}|} * (\Delta-d)^{|V_{\operatorname*{high}}|} \geq \left( \left\lfloor\frac{\Delta-q}{2}\right\rfloor + 1\right)^{\frac{q}{\Delta+q}|V(G)|}.
  \]
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md: Notice that for $q = 1$, after substituting and accounting for the parity of~$\Delta$ we obtain a bound of $\left(\left\lceil \frac{\Delta}{2}\right\rceil\right)^{\frac{1}{\Delta+1}|V(G)|}$. Meanwhile, for $q = \Delta - 2$, the bound becomes $2^{\frac{\Delta - 2}{2\Delta - 2}|V(G)|}$.
head: environment

label: rem:unique-cols
title: Remark
body_md: \label{rem:unique-cols} Note that throughout this paper, two colorings that lead to the same partition and differ only up to permutation of colors are considered distinct. To avoid this, we can color each of the first $\Delta$ vertices with a different color and only start counting colorings afterwards. This gives us a slightly weaker bound of $\left(\left\lfloor\frac{\Delta-q}{2}\right\rfloor + 1\right)^{\frac{q}{\Delta+q}|V(G)| - \Delta}$ colorings. A similar analysis can be done for our later results, and we omit the details.

label: lemma:lovasz-2-connected-lemma
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemma:lovasz-2-connected-lemma}
    Let $G$ be a $2$-connected graph with minimum degree $\delta \geq 3$ which is not complete. Then $G$ contains a pair of non-adjacent vertices $u_1, u_2$ with a common neighbor such that $G - \{u_1, u_2\}$ is connected.
head: environment

label: lemma:non-cutset-ordering
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We begin by ordering the vertices of $G - X$ by breadth-first traversal from $v$, and then taking the reverse of this order so that $v$ is rightmost.
  We prepend the vertices of $X$ to the left end of the ordering. Thus, Properties (1) and (2) are immediate from the construction.
  Property (3) holds for $u \in X$ because each such $u$ has at most $|X| - 1 < \Delta$ vertices to its left, and hence $\deg_G^\ell(u) < \Delta$.
  For $u \in V(G) \setminus (X \cup \{v\})$, Property (3) holds because our breadth-first construction ensures that $u$ has at least one neighbor to its right, and hence at most $\Delta - 1$ neighbors to its left.
head: environment

label: thm:quantbrooks
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:quantbrooks}
  Let $G$ be a connected graph of maximum degree $\Delta \geq 3$ that is not a complete graph, and let $q < \Delta$. Then, $G$ has at least~$\frac{1}{\Delta}\cdot\left(\left\lfloor\frac{\Delta-q}{2}\right\rfloor + 1\right)^{\frac{q}{\Delta + q}|V(G)| - 1}$ proper $\Delta$-colorings.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $G$ be a graph of maximum degree~$\Delta$.
  If $G$ is $d$-degenerate for some $d < \Delta$, we apply Lemma~\ref{lem-kdeg2} where $L(v) = [\Delta]$ for all $v \in V(G)$.
Hence, we are left with the case where $G$ is $\Delta$-regular.
We distinguish two cases.

  \medskip \noindent \textcolor{lipicsGray}{{\sffamily\bfseries Case 1.}} $G$ has a cut-vertex $v$.\\
  Let $G'_1, \dots , G'_r$ be the connected components of $G-v$.
    Let $G_1 = G[V(G'_1) \cup \{v\}]$ and let $G_2 = G[\bigcup_{i = 2}^{r}V(G'_i)\cup \{v\}]$.
    By \cref{obs-reg-vertremoval-deg}, we obtain that $G_1$ and $G_2$ are both $d_i$-degenerate for some $d_i < \Delta$.
  We set $L(u) = [\Delta]$ for every $u \in V(G)$ and apply Lemma~\ref{lem-kdeg2} to each $G_i$. We thus obtain that each $G_i$ has at least $\left(\left\lfloor\frac{\Delta-q}{2}\right\rfloor + 1\right)^{\frac{q}{\Delta + q}|V(G_i)|}$ proper $\Delta$-colorings.
  Since $G_1$ and $G_2$ share exactly one vertex $v$, we can only combine colorings of $G_1$ and $G_2$ in which $v$ has the same color in both colorings. Since we can permute color classes, a $\frac{1}{\Delta}$-fraction of the colorings assign $v$ a specific color $c$.
  Thus, for every fixed coloring of $G_2$, a $\frac{1}{\Delta}$-fraction of the colorings of $G_1$ give the same color to $v$. 
  Hence, the total number of proper $\Delta$-colorings of $G$ is at least 
  \[\left(\frac{1}{\Delta}\right)\cdot\left(\left\lfloor\frac{\Delta-q}{2}\right\rfloor + 1\right)^{\frac{q}{\Delta + q}(|V(G_1)|+|V(G_2)|)} \geq \left(\frac{1}{\Delta}\right)\cdot\left(\left\lfloor\frac{\Delta-q}{2}\right\rfloor + 1\right)^{\frac{q}{\Delta + q}(|V(G)| + 1)}\]





\medskip \noindent \textcolor{lipicsGray}{{\sffamily\bfseries Case 2.}} $G$ is $2$-connected.\\
Let $v$ be a vertex with two non-adjacent neighbors $u_1, u_2$ such that $G - \{u_1, u_2\}$ is connected. 
Such vertices exist by Lemma~\ref{lemma:lovasz-2-connected-lemma}, which holds since $G$ is $\Delta$-regular for $\Delta \geq 3$.
Then let $\sigma$ be the vertex ordering given by~\Cref{lemma:non-cutset-ordering} for $X = \{u_1, u_2\}$, and assume without loss of generality that $u_1$ appears to the left of $u_2$.
We apply~\Cref{lem-highlow2} to $G$ with this ordering and with the parameter $k = \Delta$.
Thus, for the set $V_{\operatorname*{low}} = \{v : \deg_G^\ell(v) < \frac{\Delta + q}{2}\}$, we have the bound $|V_{\operatorname*{low}}| \geq \frac{q}{\Delta + q}|V(G)|$.

We now count colorings by an argument similar to that of~\Cref{lem-kdeg2}.
We process the vertices in the order given by $\sigma$, with the restriction that $u_1$ and $u_2$ receive the same color. This is always possible, since they are non-adjacent by definition and since they are the first two vertices to be colored by Property (1) of~\Cref{lemma:non-cutset-ordering}.
This restriction ensures that~$v$ always has an available color, since two of its neighbors receive the same color.
Every other vertex also always has an available color, by Property (3) of~\Cref{lemma:non-cutset-ordering}.
Furthermore, every vertex in $V_{\operatorname*{low}}$ (except $u_2$, which is forced to receive the same color as $u_1$) has at least $\left\lfloor\frac{\Delta-q}{2}\right\rfloor + 1$ available colors.
Then the total number of proper colorings is at least
\[\left(\left\lfloor\frac{\Delta-q}{2}\right\rfloor + 1\right)^{|V_{\operatorname*{low}} \setminus \{u_2\}|}
   \geq \left(\left\lfloor\frac{\Delta-q}{2}\right\rfloor + 1\right)^{\frac{q}{\Delta+q}|V(G)| - 1}.\]

The result now follows from a pessimistic combination of the bounds from these cases.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
Notice that when $q = 1$, after substituting and accounting for the parity of $\Delta$, we obtain the bound
    \[
      \left(\frac{1}{\Delta}\right)\cdot\left(\left\lceil \frac{\Delta}{2} \right\rceil\right)^{\frac{|V(G)|}{\Delta + 1} - 1} \geq \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)\cdot\left(\left\lceil \frac{\Delta}{2} \right\rceil\right)^{\frac{|V(G)|}{\Delta + 1} - 2} \geq \left(\left\lceil \frac{\Delta}{2} \right\rceil\right)^{\frac{|V(G)|}{\Delta + 1}-3}.
    \]
    Furthermore, when $q = \Delta - 2$, we obtain the bound
    \[
      \frac{1}{\Delta}\cdot2^{\frac{\Delta - 2}{2\Delta - 2}|V(G)| - 1} = 2^{\frac{\Delta - 2}{2\Delta - 2}|V(G)| -1 - \log \Delta}.
    \]
head: environment

title: Theorem
body_md: Let $G$ be a connected graph of maximum degree~$\Delta$, that is not a complete graph, and let $L$, be any $\Delta$-list assignment for $G$. Let $q < \Delta$. Then, $G$ has at least $\frac{1}{\Delta}\cdot\left(\left\lfloor\frac{\Delta-q}{2}\right\rfloor + 1\right)^{\frac{q}{\Delta + q}|V(G)| - 1}$ $L$-colorings.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
If $G$ is $d$-degenerate for some $d < \Delta$, then we apply Lemma~\ref{lem-kdeg2}.
  Hence, we are left with the case where $G$ is $\Delta$-regular. 
  Similarly, if even one vertex~$v$ has $|L(v)| > \Delta$, then we apply~\Cref{lemma:non-cutset-ordering}, with $X$ being the emptyset, to obtain a vertex ordering with $v$ rightmost. The result then follows by an argument conceptually identical to that in~\Cref{lem-kdeg2}, noting that $v$ always has an available color because its list is larger than its neighborhood.
  Hence, we may assume that every list has length exactly $\Delta$.
  
  If all lists are identical, then since we consider lists of length $\Delta$ we can use the same arguments as in Theorem~\ref{thm:quantbrooks}.
  We may therefore assume that not all lists are identical.
  Thus, since $G$ is connected there exist adjacent vertices $u,v \in V(G)$ with $c_u \in L(u) \setminus L(v)$ and $c_v \in L(v)\setminus L(u)$. We distinguish two cases based on whether both $u$ and $v$ are a cut-vertex.



\medskip \noindent \textcolor{lipicsGray}{{\sffamily\bfseries Case 1.}} There are $u,v$ such that at most one of $u,v$ is a cut-vertex.\\
  Suppose that at least one of $u,v$ is not a cut-vertex, say $u$, so $G - u$ is connected. 
  Then we apply~\Cref{lemma:non-cutset-ordering} to obtain a vertex ordering $\sigma$ with $u$ leftmost, $v$ rightmost, and every vertex $w \neq v$ having $\deg_G^\ell(w) < \Delta$.
  With respect to this ordering, let $V_{\operatorname*{low}} = \{w: 0 \leq \deg_G^\ell(w) < \frac{\Delta + q}{2}\}$. By applying~\Cref{lem-highlow2} with $k = \Delta$, we have that $|V_{\operatorname*{low}}| \geq \frac{q}{\Delta + q}|V(G)|$.

  To count the number of colorings, we proceed as in the proof of~\Cref{lem-kdeg2}, processing the vertices from left to right in $\sigma$. 
  We fix the color of $u$ to be $c_u$. 
  For each following vertex, we check which colors are available.
  For each vertex $w \neq v$, there is a color available, by Property (3) of~\Cref{lemma:non-cutset-ordering}. Furthermore,~$v$ has an available color because we fixed color $c_u \notin L(v)$ for $u$, which neighbors $v$.
  
  For every $w \in V_{\operatorname*{low}}$, except $u$ for which the color $c_u$ is fixed, there are at least~$\left\lfloor \Delta - \frac{\Delta + q}{2}\right\rfloor + 1$ colors available.
  It follows that the number of $L$-colorings of $G$ is at least
  \[
    \left(\left\lfloor \Delta - \frac{\Delta + q}{2}\right\rfloor + 1\right)^{|V_{\operatorname*{low}} \setminus \{u\}|} \geq \left(\left\lfloor\frac{\Delta -q}{2}\right\rfloor + 1\right)^{\frac{q}{\Delta+q}|V(G)|-1}.
  \]

  
\medskip \noindent \textcolor{lipicsGray}{{\sffamily\bfseries Case 2.}} Both $u,v$ are cut-vertices in $G$.\\
Suppose there are no vertices $u',v' \in V(G)$ such that we can apply Case~1.
This implies that every non-cut-vertex has the same list of colors as all of its neighbors.
Since we assume that not all lists are identical, we may assume that $G$ is not $2$-connected.


We consider the block-cut-tree\xspace of $G$.
Let $B$ be a leaf block of $G$. Hence, by definition, $B$ contains only one cut-vertex $x$.
Then, all neighbors of $x$ in $B$ have the same list as $x$. It follows that all vertices in $B$ have the same list.

  Let $G' = G - (B - x)$, that is, we delete all vertices in $B$ except $x$. Notice that $G'$ is connected, and in $G'$ $x$ has degree at most $\Delta-1$.
  By \cref{lemma:non-cutset-ordering}, with $X$ being the emptyset, we obtain a $(\Delta-1)$-degeneracy ordering of $G'$ where $x$ is rightmost. 
  Using~\Cref{lem-kdeg2}, $G'$ has at least $\left(\left\lfloor\frac{\Delta-q}{2}\right\rfloor + 1\right)^{\frac{q}{\Delta + q}|V(G')|}$ $L$-colorings.

  Consider a fixed $L$-coloring of $G'$. This coloring may be combined with any $L$-coloring of~$B$ to form an $L$-coloring of $G$, as long as $x$ receives the same color in both colorings.
  Since all vertices in $B$ have the same list, we may permute color classes to see that a $\frac{1}{\Delta}$-fraction of $L$-colorings of $B$ may be combined with any given $L$-coloring of $G'$.
  Again using~\Cref{lem-kdeg2} to give a bound on the number of $L$-colorings of $B$, we now have that the total number of $L$-colorings of $G$ is at least
  \[
    \left(\frac{1}{\Delta}\right)\left(\left\lfloor\frac{\Delta-q}{2}\right\rfloor + 1\right)^{\frac{q}{\Delta + q}(|V(G')| + |V(B)|)} = \left(\frac{1}{\Delta}\right)\left(\left\lfloor\frac{\Delta-q}{2}\right\rfloor + 1\right)^{\frac{q}{\Delta + q}(|V(G)|+1)}.
  \]
  The result now follows by a pessimistic combination of the bounds in these cases.

label: thm:quantitative-degree-choosability-theorem
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:quantitative-degree-choosability-theorem}
    Let $G$ be a connected graph which is not a Gallai tree, and $L$ be any degree-list assignment. Then $G$ admits at least $2^{\frac{|V(G)| - h({G}) - b({G})}{c^*({G})-1} + 1}$ $L$-colorings.
head: environment

label: prop:rubin-subgraphs-two-colorings
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:rubin-subgraphs-two-colorings}
    Let $H$ be a Rubin graph, and let $L$ be any degree-list assignment. Then~$H$ admits at least~$2$ $L$-colorings.
head: environment

label: lemma:degree-choice:main-ordering
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $H$ be a minimum Rubin subgraph of $G$.
    We will build a vertex ordering $\sigma$ from left-to-right. We begin by ordering the vertices of $H$ arbitrarily. We will order the remaining vertices by appending to the right of this order, so that Property (1) of the lemma is satisfied. 
    
    We now say that vertices already added to our ordering $\sigma$ are \emph{ordered} and all other vertices are \emph{unordered}. While not all vertices are ordered, we select an edge $uv$ with one ordered endvertex $u$ and one unordered endvertex $v$. There is always an available choice, since $G$ is connected.
    If the edge $uv$ is a bridge, we say that $uv$ was a \emph{bad choice}; otherwise, $uv$ was a \emph{good choice}. We now describe how to add vertices to our ordering according to these two possibilities.
    
    First suppose that $uv$ was a bad choice; see Lines~\ref{line:bridge-beginning}-\ref{line:bridge-end} in~\Cref{alg:degree-choice:main-ordering-alg}. We add $v$ to our ordering (on the right). 
    Notice that we have maintained Property (2) of the lemma, since $u$ was already ordered.

    Now suppose instead that $uv$ was a good choice; see Lines~\ref{line:good-choice-beginning}-\ref{line:good-choice-end} in~\Cref{alg:degree-choice:main-ordering-alg}. 
    Let $u, w_1, \ldots, w_p, v$ be a shortest $uv$-path in $G - uv$. Such a path exists by definition of a good choice ($uv$ is not a bridge).
    For each $i \in [p]$, we add $w_i$ to our order, unless it is already ordered.
    Lastly, we add $v$ to our order.
    Notice again that we have maintained Property~(2) of the lemma, since $w_{i - 1}$ is added to the order before $w_i$ for every $i \geq 1$.
    Moreover, $\deg_G^\ell(v) \geq 2$ since both $u$ and $w_p$ are neighbors of $v$ appearing to its left in $\sigma$.
    
    This completes the ordering algorithm. It remains to show that Property (3) is satisfied.
    We observe first that upon each bad choice, exactly one unordered vertex becomes ordered, and we cannot make more than $b({G})$ bad choices.
    Then the remaining $|V(G)| - h({G}) - b({G})$ vertices are ordered via good choices. We have already shown that each good choice produces at least one vertex in~$V_{\operatorname*{low}}$.
    Then it suffices to show that upon each good choice, at most $c^*({G}) - 1$ unordered vertices become ordered.

    To see this, observe that upon a good choice $uv$, by combining the edge $uv$ with the path $u, w_1, \ldots, w_p, v$ we obtain a cycle in $G$. 
    Moreover, this cycle is induced, since $u, w_1, \ldots, w_p, v$ was chosen to be a shortest $uv$-path in $G - uv$.
    Thus, $p \leq c^*({G}) - 2$, and the result follows.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $G$ be a connected graph which is not a Gallai tree, and let $H$ be a minimum Rubin subgraph. Let $\sigma$ be an ordering of the vertices given by~\Cref{lemma:degree-choice:main-ordering}. Let $V_{\operatorname*{low}}$ be the set given by Property (3) of~\Cref{lemma:degree-choice:main-ordering}, and let $L_{G - H}$ be the restriction of $L$ to $V(G - H)$.
    Suppose we color the vertices of $G - H$ in the reverse of $\sigma$ (i.e., right-to-left).                                                                                                                             
    By Property (2) of~\Cref{lemma:degree-choice:main-ordering}, we have that for every vertex $v$ of $G - H$, there is some available color, and moreover for every $v \in V_{\operatorname*{low}}$ there are at least $2$ colors available. 
    Thus, using Property (3), the number of possible greedy $L_{G-H}$-colorings of $G - H$ is at least
    \[
        2^{|V_{\operatorname*{low}}|} \geq 2^\frac{|V(G)| - |V(H)| - b({G})}{c^*({G}) - 1} = 2^\frac{|V(G)| - h({G}) - b({G})}{c^*({G}) - 1}.
    \]
    Now we complete the proof by showing that every fixed $L_{G - H}$-coloring of $G - H$ can be extended to form two unique $L$-colorings of $G$.
    Fix an $L_{G - H}$-coloring of $G-H$, and call this coloring $\phi$. For each $v \in V(H)$, let $L^*(v) \coloneqq L(v) \setminus \{ \phi(u) : u \in N_G(v) \setminus V(H) \}$. Notice that since $|L(v)| \geq \deg_G(v)$, we have $|L^*(v)| \geq \deg_H(v)$ for every $v \in V(H)$. Thus, $L^*$ is a degree-list assignment for $H$.
    Furthermore, any $L^*$-coloring of $H$ can be combined with $\phi$ to form a unique $L$-coloring of $G$.
    By~\Cref{prop:rubin-subgraphs-two-colorings}, there are at least $2$ $L^*$-colorings of $H$. This completes the proof.

label: lemma:chordal-graphs-degree-choosable
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemma:chordal-graphs-degree-choosable}
    Let $G$ be a connected chordal graph. If $G$ is not a Gallai tree, then $G$ contains a diamond as an induced subgraph.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $G$ is not a Gallai tree, let $B$ be a block of $G$ which is neither a clique nor an odd cycle. Since $B$ is not a clique, let $u, v \in V(B)$ be a pair of vertices with distance $2$, and let $w$ be a mutual neighbor of $u$ and $v$. Let $P = u, \ldots, v$ be a shortest $uv$-path in $B - w$. Note that by our choice of $u$ and $v$, there is at least one internal vertex on $P$. Furthermore, since $P$ is a shortest path, it is an induced path.
    We observe further that $u, P, v, w, u$ is a cycle in $G$ of length at least $4$, and its only possible chords are edges linking $w$ with the internal vertices of $P$. 
    Since $G$ is chordal, every such chord exists, i.e., $w$ is adjacent to every vertex on $P$.
    Then let $u, z_1, z_2$ be the first three vertices of $P$ (it is possible that $z_2 = v$). Since $w$ is adjacent to each of these vertices, the induced subgraph $G[\{u, z_1, z_2, w\}]$ is a diamond.
head: environment

label: lemma:degree-plus-one-choosable
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemma:degree-plus-one-choosable}
    Let $G$ be a connected graph, and let $L$ be a list assignment with $|L(v)| \geq \deg(v)$ for every vertex $v$. If there exists a vertex $w$ with $|L(w)| > \deg(w)$, then $G$ admits an $L$-coloring.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: Order the vertices left to right, beginning with $w$, in increasing order of distance from $w$. Then greedily color from right to left. This is possible, since every vertex except~$w$ has at least one neighbor ordered to its left, and thus an available color, while $w$ can be colored since its list is larger than its neighborhood.

label: lemma:2-connected-unequal-degree-choosable
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemma:2-connected-unequal-degree-choosable}
    Let $G$ be a 2-connected graph, and let $L$ be a list assignment with $|L(v)| \geq \deg(v)$ for every vertex $v$. If the lists assigned by $L$ are not all pairwise equal, then $G$ admits an $L$-coloring.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: Since $G$ is connected and the lists assigned by $L$ are not all pairwise equal, there exist adjacent vertices $u, v$ and a color $c$ with $c \in L(u) \setminus L(v)$. Order the vertices left to right, beginning with $v$, in increasing order of distance from $v$ in $G - u$. Order $u$ rightmost. Because $G$ is $2$-connected, all vertices except $v$ have at least one neighbor to the left. Fix color $c$ for $u$, and then color greedily from right to left. As its neighbor $u$ received color $c \notin L(v)$, $v$ will have an available color.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By~\cite{erdos1979choosability}, Gallai trees are not degree-choosable. Then it suffices to show that if $G$ is a connected graph and not a Gallai tree, $G$ is degree-choosable. Assume otherwise, and let $G$ be a counterexample with a minimum number of vertices. Let $L$ be a list assignment for $G$ with $|L(v)| \geq \deg(v)$ for all $v$, such that $G$ admits no $L$-coloring. Let $B$ be a block of $G$ which is neither a clique nor an odd cycle. By~\Cref{prop:rubin-subgraphs}, $B$ has no Rubin subgraph, as otherwise $G$ would have one as well. Then by~\Cref{lemma:chordal-graphs-degree-choosable}, $B$ is not chordal, so $B$ contains an odd induced cycle $C = v_1, v_2, \ldots, v_k, v_1$ of length $k \geq 5$.

    Since $B \neq C$, assume without loss of generality that $v_1$ has at least one neighbor in $B \setminus C$. Among all such neighbors of $v_1$, let $x$ be one with minimum distance to $C - v_1$ in $B - v_1$. Let $P = x, \ldots, v_i$ be a shortest path from $x$ to $C - v_1$ in $B - v_1$. Let $y$ be $v_i$'s neighbor on~$P$ (it is possible that $y = x$).
    Note that by our choice of $x$, $v_1$ has no neighbors among the internal vertices of $P$. Furthermore, since $P$ was chosen to be a shortest path, $y$ is the only vertex on $P$ with any neighbor on $C - v_1$. 
    
    It will be convenient to assume that $v_1$ and $v_i$ are not adjacent, i.e., $i \notin \{2, k\}$.
    To see that this assumption is safe, we begin by claiming that $y$ must have multiple neighbors on $C - v_1$.
    Otherwise, by combining the path $v_1, x, P, v_i$ with the two $v_iv_1$-paths given by the cycle $C$, we obtain a pair of induced cycles. Since $C$ is odd, one of these cycles must be even, and thus we have found a Rubin subgraph, a contradiction.
    Next, we claim that $y$ is non-adjacent to at least one of $v_2$ and $v_k$. Otherwise, if $y$ neighbors both $v_k$ and $v_2$, then the induced subgraph $G[\{v_k, v_1, v_2, y\}]$ is either a diamond (if $v_1$ and $y$ are adjacent, i.e., if $x = y$) or a $C_4$ (if $v_1$ and $y$ are not adjacent). Both are Rubin subgraphs, a contradiction.
    Thus, since $y$ has multiple neighbors along $C - v_1$ and is non-adjacent to at least one of $v_2$ and $v_k$, there must exist a neighbor of $y$ in $C - \{v_k, v_1, v_2\}$. Choosing this neighbor as $v_i$ satisfies all of the desired properties of $P$.

    We now define an auxiliary graph $H$, and an odd cycle $C_H$ in $H$. See~\Cref{fig:cycle-path-pair}.
    \begin{align*}
        H &= 
        \begin{cases}
            G \setminus \{v_{i+1}, \ldots, v_k\} + v_1v_i \quad\phantom{}\text{ if $i$ is odd.}\\
            G \setminus \{v_2, \ldots, v_{i - 1}\} + v_1v_i \quad\text{ if $i$ is even.}
        \end{cases} \\
        C_H &=
        \begin{cases}
            v_1, C, v_i, v_1 \quad\text{ if $i$ is odd.}\\
            v_i, C, v_1, v_i \quad\text{ if $i$ is even.}
        \end{cases}
    \end{align*}

body_md:
\label{lemma:irregular-degenerate} 
Let $G$ be a $d$-degenerate graph of maximum degree $\Delta$ with $d<\Delta$. Let $p=(p_1, \dots, p_s)$ be a vector of $s \geq 1$ integers with $p_i \geq 0$ for $i \in [s]$.
Let $q < \Delta$.
 If $\sum_{i=1}^{s} p_i = \Delta - s$, then $G$ admits at least $\textup{choices}_{\Delta}(p,q)^{\frac{q}{\Delta+q}|V(G)|-s}$ $p$-partitions.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $G$ be a $d$-degenerate graph for some $d < \Delta$. Fix a $d$-degeneracy ordering $\sigma$ of the vertices. We partition $V(G)$ by the left degree with respect to $\sigma$. Let $V_{\operatorname*{high}} = \{v: \frac{\Delta+ q}{2} \leq \deg_G^\ell(v) \}$, and let $V_{\operatorname*{low}} = \{v: 0 \leq \deg_G^\ell(v) <  \frac{\Delta+q}{2} \}$. Applying~\Cref{lem-highlow2} with parameter $k = \Delta$, we have $|V_{\operatorname*{low}}| \geq \frac{q}{\Delta+q}|V(G)|$. 
    
    We get a lower bound on the number of $p$-partitions into sets $\{V_1, \dots, V_s\}$ by processing the vertices in the order of $\sigma$ from left to right. First, we assign $v_i$ to $V_i$ for $i \in [s]$. Note that this ensures the obtained partitions are unique. Now, for each following $v_j$ with $j \in \{(s+1), \dots, n\}$, 
    we observe that if $v_j$ has at most $p_i$ neighbors in $V_i$, then $v_j$ can be assigned to $V_i$. If $v_j \in V_{\operatorname*{low}}$, then $\deg_G^\ell(v_j) \leq \frac{\Delta+q}{2}$. Hence, then the number of partite sets, $v_j$ can join is at least $\textup{choices}_{\Delta}(p,q)$, since $\sum_{i=1}^{\textup{choices}_{\Delta}(p,q)} (p_i +1) \geq \frac{\Delta-q}{2} = \Delta - \frac{\Delta+q}{2}$. To see this, note that if $v_j$ has $p_i+1$ neighbors in each of the $s-\textup{choices}_{\Delta}(p,q)$ smallest sets, the number of sets it can be assigned to is minimal.
    Therefore, there are at least $\textup{choices}_{\Delta}(p,q)^{|V_{\operatorname*{low}}|-s} \geq \textup{choices}_{\Delta}(p,q)^{\frac{q}{\Delta+q}|V(G)|-s}$ $p$-partitions.

\label{lemma:special-neighborhood}
    Let $G$ be a 2-connected graph distinct from $K^*_{\Delta+1}$ and $K_{\Delta+1}$ and $v \in V(G)$. Suppose all vertices in $G$ have degree $\Delta$ except possibly $v$. Then there exists a special neighborhood $(z, X)$ with $v \notin X$.

title: Proof
body_md:
Suppose $G$ is $d$-degenerate for some $d < \Delta$. Then, we apply \cref{lemma:irregular-degenerate} and obtain $\textup{choices}_{\Delta}(p,q)^{\frac{q}{\Delta+q}|V(G)|-s}$ $p$-partitions. Hence, we may assume that $G$ is $\Delta$-regular.
Let $G_1$ be a leaf block in the block-cut-tree of $G$. Note that $G_1$ = $G$ if $G$ is 2-connected. We distinguish two cases.
    
    \medskip \noindent \textcolor{lipicsGray}{{\sffamily\bfseries Case 1.}} $G_1$ is a quasi-clique.\\
    Since $G_1$ is not $\Delta$-regular, $G_1 \neq G$. Let $u \in V(G_1)$ be the single cut vertex of $G_1$. 
    Let $G_2 = G - (V(G_1) \setminus \{u\})$.
    Since $G_1$ is a quasi-clique and $u$ has a neighbor in $G_2$, $\deg_{G_1}(u)=2$, and since $G$ is $\Delta$-regular, for all $v \in V(G_1) \setminus \{u\}$, we get $\deg_{G_1}(v)= \Delta$. 
    By \cref{obs-reg-vertremoval-deg}, $G_2$ is $(\Delta-1)$-degenerate, so by \cref{lemma:irregular-degenerate}, there are $\textup{choices}_{\Delta}(p,q)^{\frac{q}{\Delta+q}|V(G_2)|-s}$ $p$-partitions of $G_2$.
    Fix some $p$-partition $\mathcal{P}_{G_2}=\{V_1, \dots, V_s\}$ of $G_2$. We will get a lower bound on the number of partitions in $G_1$ compatible with $\mathcal{P}_{G_2}$.
    
    We construct an ordering of the vertices in $G_1$. Let $x,y$ be the neighbors of $u$ in $G_1$ and let $X = \{u, x,y\}$. We apply \cref{lemma:non-cutset-ordering} to $G_1$ and $X$ and obtain an ordering $\sigma$ where the vertices in $X$ are the leftmost vertices. Let $v$ be the rightmost vertex according to $\sigma$. We order the vertices in $X$ $u,x,y$. Note that this does not influence the properties of the ordering obtained by \cref{lemma:non-cutset-ordering}.
    We apply \cref{lem-highlow2} to $G_1$ with ordering $\sigma$ and obtain that $|V_{\operatorname*{low}}| \geq \frac{q}{\Delta+q}|V(G_1)|$, for $V_{\operatorname*{low}} = \{v: 0 \leq \deg_{G_1}^\ell(v) < \frac{\Delta+q}{2} \}$.
    
    To count the number of partitions of $G_1$, we use an argument similar to \cref{lemma:irregular-degenerate}. We process the vertices in the order given by $\sigma$. Since we want to extend a partition of $G_2$ and $u \in V(G_1) \cap V(G_2)$, we assign $u$ to the same set as for $G_2$. Next, we assign $x$ to a different set than the one containing $u$; any set will do, since $u$ is the only neighbor of $x$ which has already been assigned. Further, we assign $y$ to the same set as $x$, which is once again possible because $u$ is the only neighbor of $y$ which has already been assigned.
    
    For each remaining vertex $w \neq v$, there is guaranteed to be at least one available set $V_i$ with at most $p_i$ left neighbors of $w$, since each such $w$ has left degree less than $\Delta$ by Property (3) of~\Cref{lem-highlow2}.

    It remains to show that we can safely add the righmost vertex $v$ to some set. Let $V_i$ be the set containing both $x$ and $y$. If $p_i = 0$, then there must be an available set for $v$ because $V_i$ contains $p_i + 2$ neighbors of $v$.
    Then we may assume that $p_i > 0$. In this case, we add $v$ to $V_i$. To see that $G[V_i]$ remains $p_i$-degenerate, observe that $|V_i \setminus \{v\}| \leq p_i + 1$, as otherwise we have contradicted our greedy coloring procedure (since $G_1$ is a quasi-clique). Then $|V_i| \leq p_i + 2$. A $p_i$-degeneracy ordering may be obtained by taking an arbitrary order with $x$ rightmost. Since $|V_i| \leq p_i + 2$, it is immediate that every vertex except $x$ has at most $p_i$ left neighbors. Meanwhile, $x$ has at most $p_i$ left neighbors because it is non-adjacent to $y$.

    Thus, for each partition of $G_2$, there are at least $\textup{choices}_{\Delta}(p,q)^{\frac{q}{\Delta+q}|V(G_1)|-3}$ partitions of $G_1$ that extend that of $G_2$.
    It follows that the total the number of $p$-partitions of $G$ is at least 
    \[\left( \textup{choices}_{\Delta}(p,q)^{\frac{q}{\Delta+q}|V(G_2)|-s} \right) \left( \textup{choices}_{\Delta}(p,q)^{\frac{q}{\Delta+q}|V(G_1)|-3} \right) = \textup{choices}_{\Delta}(p,q)^{\frac{q}{\Delta+q}|V(G)|-s-3}.\] 
    

    \medskip \noindent \textcolor{lipicsGray}{{\sffamily\bfseries Case 2.}} $G_1$ is not a quasi-clique.\\
    If $G \neq G_1$, then let $v \in G_1$ be the single cut vertex of $G$. Otherwise, let $v$ be any vertex of~$G_1$.
    By \cref{lemma:special-neighborhood}, since $G_1$ is neither complete nor a quasi-clique there exists $z \in V(G_1)$ and $X \subseteq G_1$ such that $(z, X)$ is a special neighborhood in $G_1$ with $v \notin X$. Since $v \notin X$, and $G_1-X$ is connected, $G-X$ is connected. Let $x, y \in X$ be two non-adjacent vertices that exist by definition of $X$. We apply \cref{lemma:non-cutset-ordering} to $G$, $X$ and $z$ and find an ordering~$\sigma$ with $z$ as the rightmost vertex. We let $x,y$ be the leftmost vertices of $X$ in $\sigma$.
     We partition the vertices of $G$ based on their left degree in $\sigma$. Let $V_{\operatorname*{high}} = \{v: \frac{\Delta + q}{2}  \leq \deg_{G}^\ell(v) \}$, and let $V_{\operatorname*{low}} = \{v: 0 \leq \deg_{G}^\ell(v) < \frac{\Delta+q}{2} \}$. By Lemma~\ref{lem-highlow2}, $|V_{\operatorname*{low}}| \geq \frac{q}{\Delta+q}|V(G)|$.

    We get a lower bound on the number of $p$-partitions of $G$ by processing the vertices in the order of $\sigma = v_1, \dots, v_n$ from left to right.
    We assign $x,y$ as well as $v_3, \dots, v_{p_s+2}$ to $V_s$. Note that $V_s$ is $p_s$-degenerate, by the same argument as given in Case 1, since $x$ and $y$ are non-adjacent. Further, for $i \in \{1,\dots, s-1\}$, we assign $v_{p_s + i + 2}$ to $V_i$. For all following vertices, similar to Case~1, there are at least $\textup{choices}_{\Delta}(p,q)$ partite sets a vertex in $V_{\operatorname*{low}}$ can be assigned to, and at least one set a vertex in $V_{\operatorname*{high}}$ can be assigned to.
    Finally, since $z$ has $p_s+2$ neighbors in $V_s$ and $\sum_{i=1}^s(p_i+1) = \Delta$, there is some set $V_i$ containing at most $p_i$ neighbors of $z$.
    So we can safely assign $z$ to $V_i$.

    Hence, the number of $p$-partitions of $G$ is at least 
    \[\textup{choices}_{\Delta}(p,q)^{|V_{\operatorname*{low}}| - (p_s + s+1)} \geq \textup{choices}_{\Delta}(p,q)^{\frac{q}{\Delta+q}|V(G)|- p_s-s -1} .\]

    \noindent
    The result now follows by a pessimistic combination of the bounds obtained in the two cases.

title: Remark
body_md: If $p_i = d$ for $d \leq \frac{\Delta}{2}$, for all $i \in [s]$, then for $q=1$, we obtain that $\textup{choices}_{\Delta}(p,1) = \lceil \frac{s}{2}\rceil$. Hence, the number of partitions is at least $\lceil\frac{s}{2}\rceil^{\frac{|V(G)|}{\Delta+1} - d-s -3}$. Setting $d = 0$, that is, requiring the partition to be a coloring, we recover (up to the additive constant) our bound from \cref{thm:quantbrooks} in the modified version for unique colorings, see \cref{rem:unique-cols}.

body_md: \textsc{$p$-\textsc{Degenerate Partitioning}\xspace}, for $p = (p_1, p_2) \neq (1, 1)$, is \textnormal{\textsf{NP}}-complete for graphs of maximum degree $\Delta = p_1 + p_2 + 3 \geq 5$.

label: thm:molloy-hardness
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:molloy-hardness}
    Let $\Delta \geq 3$ and let $k_\Delta$ be the maximum integer such that $\Delta \geq (k_\Delta+1)(k_\Delta+2)$. For every $3 \leq k \leq \Delta-k_\Delta-1$, \textsl{$k$-\textsc{Colorability}\xspace} is \textnormal{\textsf{NP}}-complete for graphs of maximum degree $\Delta$.
head: environment

label: cor-coloringhardbound
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor-coloringhardbound}
    For every integer $k \geq 3$ and $\Delta \geq \left(\frac{1}{2} + \frac{\sqrt{4k+1}}{2}\right)^2$, \textsl{$k$-\textsc{Colorability}\xspace} is \textnormal{\textsf{NP}}-complete for graphs with maximum degree $\Delta$.

body_md:
\label{clm: external_same}
    Let $S_v$ be a vertex gadget in $H$. The external vertices of $S_v$ belong to the same set in $\mathcal{P}$.

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $x$ and $y$ be the external vertices of $S_v$ with $x \in V_i$ and $y \in V_j$ for $i, j \in [s]$. Suppose toward a contradiction that $i \neq j$.
    If $V_i$ contains $p_i+1$ clique vertices of $S_v$, then the subgraph induced on $x$ and all clique vertices of $S_v$ in $V_i$ have minimum degree at least~$p_i+1$. Hence, at most $p_i$ clique vertices of $S_v$ are in $V_i$. 
    Likewise, at most $p_j$ clique vertices in $S_v$ are in $V_j$.
    Similarly, if there were $p_h+2$ clique vertices in $V_h$ for $h \in [s]$, $h\neq i, j$, then the subgraph induced on the clique vertices of $S_v$ in $V_k$ has minimum degree at least~$p_h+1$. Hence, at most $p_h+1$ clique vertices of $S_v$ are in $V_h$. Since
     \[\sum_{h=1, h \neq i,j}^s (p_h+1) + p_i + p_j = \sum_{i=1}^s p_i+s-2 < \sum_{i=1}^s p_i +s -1,\]
     there is a clique vertex of $S_v$ which is not contained in a set of $\mathcal{P}$, contradicting the fact that $\mathcal{P}$ is a partition.

title: Proof
body_md:
First, note that by the definition in the statement of~\Cref{thm:molloy-hardness}, we have $\Delta \geq (k_\Delta + 1)(k_\Delta + 2)$. It follows that
    \[
        \sqrt{\Delta} \geq \sqrt{(k_\Delta + 1)(k_\Delta + 2)} > k_\Delta + 1.
    \]
    That is, we have $k_\Delta < \sqrt{\Delta} - 1$. Now, let $k$ be any value such that $3 \leq k \leq \Delta - (\sqrt{\Delta} - 1) - 1$. By substituting $k_\Delta < \sqrt{\Delta} - 1$, we obtain that for all such $k$, $k \leq \Delta - k_\Delta - 1$. After rearranging and applying~\Cref{thm:molloy-hardness}, we have that $k$-\textsc{Colorability}\xspace is \textnormal{\textsf{NP}}-hard whenever $k \geq 3$ and $\Delta \geq k + (\sqrt{\Delta} - 1) + 1 = k + \sqrt{\Delta}$.
    For a fixed $k \geq 3$, to find the minimum~$\Delta$ for which this inequality holds we need to solve the equation $\Delta_0 = k + \sqrt{\Delta_0}$. The solution is
    \[ \Delta_0 = \left(\frac{1}{2} + \frac{\sqrt{4k+1}}{2}\right)^2.\]
